_readme: An entry clears exactly ONE deploy from the exit code. It never hides it: an acknowledged
deploy is still printed in full on every fire, tagged with the issue that settled it, and
`pnpm check:deploy-origin -- --no-acks` prints the raw truth with every ack ignored.
Matching is by EXACT `deployId`. There is deliberately no way to ack a CLASS: an entry that
said 'manual is fine' would re-create the unenforced convention this detector replaced.
An entry needs `deployId`, `issue`, `reviewedAt` and `why`. An entry missing any of those
does NOT apply -- the deploy alarms as an ordinary bypass and the run prints a WARNING
naming the incomplete entry. Fail closed.
⛔ THESE ACKS ARE WEAKER THAN `scripts/boot-arm-repair-acks.json`'s, AND DELIBERATELY SO.
That ledger demands a `fixCommit` that made recurrence impossible. There is no such commit
here and there cannot be one: the hole is a permissions hole on Render's dashboard, and the
workspace's only member is its own ADMIN (measured 2026-09-23: GET /v1/owners/tea-d7macfog4nts73ai6p40/members
returns exactly one row, eetiennecg@gmail.com, role ADMIN). An ack here means 'seen, reviewed,
dispositioned on a ticket' and nothing more. Do not import the stronger ledger's semantics.
Acking is not the remedy. Each entry should name the issue where the deploy was actually
adjudicated, so the ledger reads as a list of decisions rather than a list of dismissals.

acks.why: Adjudicated: it was an ENV-VAR write, not a settings write. Render's markers are disjoint and this row carries envUpdated:true with NO updatedProperty -- and there is not one updatedProperty row in the entire 2000-event corpus (2026-07-10..09-23), so VERB 2 is ruled out by Render's own labelling, not by inference from the label alone. The trigger object is byte-identical to dep-d9h1j5nlk1mc738s57qg (2026-07-23), the row ENV_WRITE_TRUTH itself cites as the canonical env-write occurrence. NOT an agent: no heartbeat run existed anywhere in the company at the instant (nearest ended 09-20T22:21:00Z, next began 09-21T10:15:27Z, n=0 in flight), and 0 of 3 recent single-key API env writes (09-19 x2, 09-20 x1) produced any deploy -- so TRA-3724's measurement holds for the API verb and the write came through another surface (dashboard, or the banned full-set PUT). WHICH surface and WHICH key are UNREAD and unreadable: GET /env-vars returns {key,value} only, with no timestamp or actor. Cost: none -- but NOT because Render pinned. 9472ced3 was the branch TIP from 09-20T21:57:16Z to 09-22T19:33:37Z (45h36m, nothing pushed to main), so tip-semantics and serving-semantics were the same SHA and this row cannot discriminate them. Had anything landed on main in those 4h11m it would have shipped unguarded. Acked because it is adjudicated, not because it is safe: no gate is available for the surface that produced it (same one-ADMIN-member hole measured on TRA-4789), so this detector remains the only control. ENV_WRITE_TRUTH and CLAUDE.md corrected in the same commit -- the falsified part was the UNQUALIFIED wording 'an env-var write does not auto-deploy', which was surface-blind.

The dashboard deploy found in the TRA-4384 freeze-sprint report §2 and the reason TRA-4789 exists. It ran none of render-redeploy.mjs's gates. Adjudicated by the CEO: it landed inside the then-active cadence ceiling and cost nothing -- luck, not a control. Acked so that the NEXT press of the button is the thing this detector reports, rather than being buried under a permanent day-one red.

Second of THREE dashboard deploys on 2026-09-13, all carrying b22a9999. TRA-4384 §2 reported one; the full history read for TRA-4789 found three (04:04Z, 04:51Z, 12:49Z). Same commit, same actor, same adjudication as the first -- all three land outside the 13:25-20:00Z RTH freeze and carry a commit that was already the deploy target.

Third of the three. 12:49Z is 36 minutes before the RTH freeze opens at 13:25Z -- the closest any of them came to a gate that would have refused, and the clearest statement of why an unenforced convention was not enough.

Adjudicated: an ENV-VAR write through a non-API surface (dashboard or the banned full-set PUT) -- envUpdated:true, no user, no updatedProperty; still zero updatedProperty rows in the corpus, so VERB 2 stays ruled out by Render's own labelling. NOT the API verb (TRA-3724 holds: 0/3 single-key writes deploy) and NOT attributable to an agent: exactly ONE heartbeat run was in flight company-wide at 16:41:06Z (CTO run 2eed1080, 16:37:45->16:46:21Z, the TRA-2111 fold ratification), a read-and-disposition run whose comment landed at 16:41:03Z -- 3 seconds before deploy_started -- with health-route reads only and no Render write in its trail; and even a single-key API write from it would not have materialised a deploy. WHICH key: unreadable (GET /env-vars has no timestamp/actor). UNLIKE the 09-21 row this one DISCRIMINATES tip vs serving, and it PINNED SERVING: it carried 7f290414 (serving since the gated 10:50:27Z api deploy dep-dapqtsrbc2fs73bo467g) while origin/main's tip was 2e6feeaa, >=11 commits ahead (e08e2d05 pushed 16:10Z, 2e6feeaa 16:34Z). That is the OPPOSITE direction from the 07-23 occurrence, which shipped the TIP over the operator's 13:23Z pin -- the surface's commit choice is now measured in BOTH directions (tip-ship n=1 Jul, serving-pin n=1 Sep, indeterminate n=1) and must be treated as UNPREDICTABLE; the treat-as-capable-of-shipping-the-tip posture stands. Both Sept rows built in 50-65s vs ~3min for api deploys, consistent with a same-image env-apply -- recorded as hypothesis, not a read. COST WAS REAL, unlike 09-21: first bypass row to land INSIDE the 13:25-20:00Z RTH freeze; it killed serving pid 76 at 5.80h uptime mid-RTH and the replacement crash-looped three times inside RTH (server_failed nonZeroExit:1 at 16:48:11 / 16:51:26 / 16:59:16Z -- the TRA-4158 boot-burst heap trips, spender #12 on that tape). Acked because adjudicated, not safe: no gate exists for this surface (the RTH freeze included), so this detector remains the only control. ENV_WRITE_TRUTH and CLAUDE.md updated with the discriminating measurement in the same commit.
